s: a steep, half-timbered Eifel town wrapped around the Rur river
w: A tightly packed cluster of slate-hung, half-timbered houses climbing the steep sides of the narrow Rur valley, largely built by wealthy cloth merchants in the 17th-18th centuries and little altered since. The scale keeps it walkable in an afternoon, while the surrounding Eifel hills offer immediate hiking straight out of town.
_facts: Historic town in the Eifel region, North Rhine-Westphalia, on the Rur river near the Belgian border
Built up largely by wealthy cloth-manufacturing families in the 17th and 18th centuries
Known for its dense concentration of well-preserved slate-and-timber-framed houses
Surrounded by Eifel National Park hiking trails
